questions.answer:

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I dont know, ive never lived on campus, not abroad and not at home, so its hard to say

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It would have been nice to know which courses you were going to get before going, especially if youre in a situation like me; I had to get some specific courses for my preapproval, as some of the courses I was supposed to have at home were mandatory - so it was a bit uncertain whether I was going to get the correct courses and even if they were going to get offered. There was one course, which for some reason only was available for Erasmus+ students, which sucked. I liked the flexibility about changing courses - it must have been nice for those who did not have to take any specific courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Be ready on the computer at a certain time, apply for the courses you want. See if you get them or not. If not you will get on the waiting list and maybe even email the lecturer to see if it is possible to join anyway. It is possible to change courses until two weeks into the semester, which I think was nice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A walkthrough of how to register before the registration itself. After registration you could email the IO or  the lecturers to see if they could help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty succesful i guess, got all the classes I needed for getting credit transfer for my mandatory courses back home, but I think it could have been done easier if I i.e. had got some of the courses which would cover for more. For my mandatory 7.5 ects course at home (DAK3), I had to have 3 different courses here (total of 17 ects) to cover it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have some mandatory courses at home, be aware that the course catalogue is not always the same as the year before - be ready to change plans. If everything is elective, enjoy that you can change courses in the first two weeks

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lower level than at home, never got so many As.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 4 MA courses, total of 23 ects points, 2 BA courses total of 9 ects points and one sports course (2 ects), but the sports course did not get transfered.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I liked the MA courses for being only 25-30 people at max, a lot of discussion. At UCPH the approach is more critical, which I kind of missed. At CU when discussing a text we mainly talked about it and did not have any sort of critic towards it. For some lecturers I think the communication was too bad - getting know you have a big assignment 10 days before you have to hand it in does not make sense in my head - why not tell in further advance? Some courses did not have syllabuses, because we have to do our own reseach - that would never happen in Cph.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: JTM254 - Promoting democracy abroad: the US and the EU in third countries: Jan Hornat was a great lecturer who made the course, which itself is interesting, even more interesting.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many sport opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you wanna talk to locals, go for a sport.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go skiing, go to the mountains on a hike at the german border - there is probably also nice at the polish border area. Go watch some football, go for the techno venues, go for cheap beers

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was alright, it is different from Denmark, but not that much.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for a sports course

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Its hard to point out specific things to be honest.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy the public transport
Go out of Prague a time or two
Dont be afraid to talk to new people - everyone's new

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some of the exams are handwritten

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new international friends but also getting really tight with my danish roommates who Ill still be seeing back home

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling alone and away from friends and family back home
